product_policy_decision.decision_summary: Intended ClineMM product contract: SESSION_OVERRIDE=ALL + effective Seatbelt confinement active => ALL means ALL for native editor tools as well. Persisted editFiles=false is a baseline/default preference, NOT a hard deny against an explicit task-scoped ALL override.
product_policy_decision.distinction: persisted editor auto-approve OFF = default preference, overridable by task-scoped ALL. Explicit disabled/forbidden tool = hard authority boundary, NOT overridden merely by ALL.
product_policy_decision.consistency_with_command_policy: ALL + Seatbelt => user delegates approval to sandbox/kernel. Explicit DENY / disabled capability remains DENY.

permission_handling_mdx.verbatim_quote_1: Tool names not listed in toolPolicies default to enabled and auto-approved, so set policies explicitly for tools that need review.
permission_handling_mdx.verbatim_quote_2: Or with ClineCore: ... toolPolicies: { run_commands: { autoApprove: true }, editor: { autoApprove: true }, read_files: { autoApprove: true }, apply_patch: { autoApprove: true }, search_codebase: { autoApprove: true }, fetch_web_content: { autoApprove: true }, }, ... // canonical 'auto-approve everything' example explicitly sets editor AND apply_patch to autoApprove: true
permission_handling_mdx.verbatim_quote_3: Auto-approving all tools means the agent can execute any shell command, modify any file, and make network requests without your review. Only use this in environments where the agent's actions are either sandboxed or fully trusted.

acp_mdx.verbatim_quote_1: Per session - sessions expose an Auto-approve tools toggle in the client's session settings ... Flipping it takes effect on the next tool call.
acp_mdx.verbatim_quote_2: With auto-approval on, Cline edits files and runs commands without asking. Only enable it in workspaces where you're comfortable with unattended changes.

product_policy_decision.explicit_deny_preserved: Explicit DENY / disabled capability remains non-overridable by ALL alone. This matches both upstream semantics and the command-policy work in this codebase.
